sources.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems (arXiv:2001.00617v2)
sources.locator: Chapter 9: Lemma 9.5 and its proof (PDF p. 85); equation (9.6); Theorem 9.8 and its complete residual-comparison proof; Theorem 9.9 and its complete local minimum-norm proof (PDF pp. 87–88); caveat immediately following Theorem 9.9.

contents.name: Equation (9.6): the one-basepoint local tangential cone condition
Theorem 9.8: two-sided comparison of the derivative and nonlinear data residual
Theorem 9.9: local uniqueness of the x0-minimum-norm solution under the TCC and orthogonality condition
Lemma 9.5: locally Lipschitz derivatives give a quadratic linearization remainder
contents.reason: The assigned theorem assumes TCC directly; this stronger derivative-regularity estimate neither implies TCC by itself nor is needed for the comparison or minimum-norm proof.

contents.name: Theorem 9.7: local ill-posedness under a locally Lipschitz derivative
contents.reason: This result concerns the relation between nonlinear and linearized ill-posedness under a separate regularity assumption, which the assigned TCC items neither state nor use.

contents.name: Caveat after Theorem 9.9: the TCC can be difficult to verify and may fail for concrete problems

sources.title: Barbara Kaltenbacher, Frank Schöpfer, and Thomas Schuster, Iterative methods for nonlinear ill-posed problems in Banach spaces: convergence and applications to parameter identification problems (University of Stuttgart Preprint 2008/005)
sources.locator: §1 operator equation F(x)=y (PDF pp. 4–5); §2.3 equation (9) and Proposition 1 with proof discussion (PDF pp. 6–7).

contents.name: Section 1: nonlinear operator equation between Banach spaces and exact data model
Section 2.3, equation (9): the two-point tangential cone condition on a set
contents.reason: The source uses a stronger uniform two-point variant; the A-page states the pointwise one-basepoint form and remarks on the distinction.

contents.name: Proposition 1: existence and uniqueness of an x0-minimum-norm solution under set-level TCC hypotheses
contents.reason: The proposition has additional Banach-space convexity, domain, and continuity assumptions and refers to earlier proofs; the A-page instead proves the local Hilbert-space claim directly from Clason Theorem 9.9.

contents.name: Section 2.3 continuity and sequential-closedness hypotheses for iterative convergence results
contents.reason: These existence and convergence hypotheses concern iterative regularization methods, none of which is stated or analyzed by the assigned local identifiability results.
